_notes: Source of truth for the v2 consent and privacy UI strings. consents[].text values are versioned legal texts: after launch never edit them; a change = a new version row in wcxb_consent_texts.
text_sha256 = lowercase hex sha256 of the exact UTF-8 bytes of text (lines joined by a single \n, no trailing newline, no HTML). Plain ASCII on purpose so the hash is stable.
The consent texts contain NO placeholders, so one text and one hash fit every plugin, website and app.

Placeholders used outside the consent texts: {plugin_name}, {plugin_version}, {email}, {date}, {year}, {privacy_url}, {privacy_email}, {contact_email}, {postal_address}, {signup_place}, {app_name}, {site_name}, {unsubscribe_link}.

Usage rendering: line 1 of consents[usage].text is the visible sentence (opt-in screen and notice); the '- ' lines are the bullets inside 'What we collect', in this order. Render them from the text itself, so what is shown is exactly what is hashed.

Marketing rendering (every newsletter form, plugin card and SaaS sign-up): lines 1 and 2 of consents[marketing].text, joined by one space, are the description (one paragraph under the heading, or the SaaS checkbox label). Line 3 is the small print, followed by one space and the small_print link. Never shorten, reorder or translate them.

Consent proof to store for marketing (single opt-in, so all of it at the Subscribe click): email, text_version, text_sha256, privacy_policy_version, consent_method ('form_submit' on forms and the plugin card, 'checkbox' in SaaS apps), source (plugin:{slug}/channel:plugin-box, site:{host}/form:inline|footer|slide-in plus the page path, app:{slug}), submitted_at (UTC), IP address and user agent of the request (for the plugin card: the admin's browser IP and user agent, passed by the client library, not the web server's). This is the GDPR Art 7(1) proof and the 'date, time, purpose and manner' record of CRTC Bulletin 2012-548.
Usage proof: site id, text_version, text_sha256, granted_at (UTC), plugin slug that showed the screen or notice, client version, privacy_policy_version.

Public paths give the SAME reply for a new, subscribed, unsubscribed or suppressed email and for honeypot hits (no enumeration). A public form never changes the name or other profile fields of an existing person; it only adds the source tag. With single opt-in a public form can NOT re-subscribe an unsubscribed or suppressed email (complained, bounced, erased): anyone could type it, and CAN-SPAM 15 U.S.C. 7704(a)(4) bars mail after an opt-out without the person's own new consent. Same reply anyway. Coming back = write to the privacy contact, or tick the box in a SaaS app with a verified account email.
The usage label is NOT 'anonymous': the payload has the site address and a site id, so it is personal data (GDPR Art 4(1), Recital 26). 'Non-sensitive' is fine (same word WooCommerce uses).
If the client starts sending a new field group, ship a new usage text version in the same release, and update readme-external-services-v2.md and the privacy policy.

Product lists (VidShop users, Media Sweep users, AI Sales Agent users, ViewMeter users) are covered by marketing line 2. Allowed inputs only: the source of the signup (plugin card of that plugin) and plugins seen on a site that shares usage data AND is linked to the person. Never link a person to a site by guessing (same host, admin email match).
No dark patterns: Allow and No thanks / Skip the same size and style; slide-in close always visible; no countdown, no guilt text; a refusal is never asked again by the same surface.
Translations: consent texts in English only in v2 (do not wrap them in __()). A translated text needs its own version and hash, for example marketing-2026-12-fr. Other UI strings may be translated.
tests/contract/fixtures/*.json and every test that pins hashes: use the two text_sha256 values below (usage unchanged, marketing new).

consents.text:
Allow WPCreatix to collect non-sensitive usage data, including the list of plugins and themes, to improve our plugins. You can turn this off anytime.
- Site: address, a random site ID, language, WordPress, PHP and MySQL versions, server type, multisite or not.
- Live, staging or local. A staging or local copy may be linked to your live site.
- Plugins and themes: name, slug, version, author, active or not.
- Our plugins: which ones, versions and install dates.
- Rounded counts, like 100-999 posts, and how often you use some of our features.
- WooCommerce: store currency and country.
- When: about once a week, and when our plugins are activated, deactivated, updated or deleted.
- Your country, read from your server's IP address. We do not store the IP.
- Never: your content, customer or order data, user names, emails or passwords.
- We never sell this data.
- Sent to WPCreatix (Wuzzify LLC, Cairo, Egypt). Covers all WPCreatix plugins on this site.

WPCreatix news, tips and offers by email.
Matched to the plugins you use.
Unsubscribe anytime.

_notes: The ONE line under every email input (plugin card, inline, footer, slide-in, SaaS checkbox): text + ' ' + a link with link_text to {privacy_url}. text MUST equal line 3 of consents[marketing].text (a unit test checks it). Nothing else in the small print: no address, no frequency, no Turnstile line.
Always visible, never in a tooltip; 13-14px, same contrast rules as body text.

The FULL-SCREEN OPT-IN (Freemius style, design 4-V2 with a SKY-BLUE #88c5ff top band instead of green). Usage only, no email. Shown INSTEAD of the plugin UI the FIRST time an admin opens one of our plugin's own admin pages, on new installs AND on existing installs after the update that adds it. NO redirect on activation. Shown once per site (the choice is shared by all WPCreatix plugins), never on the dashboard, Plugins screen or other plugins' pages (Guideline 11).

Layout: band with stub_label + WPCreatix logo; plugin icon + {plugin_name}; title; the sentence (line 1 of consents[usage].text); [Allow & Continue] [Skip] the same size; under them the collapsed 'What we collect' (bullets from the text, then preview_link) and privacy_link.

Allow & Continue = granted row for usage-2026-12-en, then open the plugin page. Skip = nothing sent (local flag only), open the plugin page with every feature working (Guideline 7). Skip is a real button, not a faint link.
update_badge + update_line: optional, only for existing installs seeing it after the update. Not hashed.
After Skip, the only other ask is optin_notice, once.

_notes: Three forms on wpcreatix.com and our other sites, all from the WPCreatix Forms embed: inline (end of blog posts and docs, design 1-V1 WITHOUT the 'WPCreatix notes' badge), footer (top of the site footer, design 2-V1 WITHOUT badge), slide_in (design 3-V2). NO centre popup. All post to Bridge with the site's form key. Source tags: website-inline, website-footer, website-slidein (plus site:{host} and the page path in the proof).
Every form: heading (per form, below) + description = marketing lines 1-2 + email field + Subscribe + small print. No checkbox.

Anti-spam: Cloudflare Turnstile (loaded when the person focuses the email field, or when the slide-in opens), honeypot, minimum fill time, MX/domain check, rate limits. The same success reply for every email; a bad domain gets email_invalid.

Slide-in rules: desktop only (viewport 1024px or wider); non-modal, bottom-right, the page stays usable; shown only after (60% scroll AND 40 s visible) OR (2nd page in the visit, read from a same-host document.referrer, AND 20 s); never before 15 s; never on privacy, terms, checkout, cart, account or contact pages (also behind a language prefix such as /de/privacy-policy/); never while the cookie banner or another overlay is open or while the person types in a field; close button visible and keyboard reachable; Esc closes.

Slide-in memory, localStorage ONLY (no cookie, no fallback; if localStorage throws, do not show the slide-in): key in storage_key, value JSON {"n":<closes>,"t":<unix day of the last close>,"s":1 after subscribe,"v":<unix minute when last shown>}. Rules: s=1 -> never show again; n=1 -> hide 30 days after t; n>=2 -> hide 90 days after t; v less than 30 minutes ago -> do not show again (one show per visit). A subscribe from the inline or footer form also sets s=1. No id, no email, never sent to any server.
